newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTO MARCH TOWARDS RECORD THIRD LEAGUE TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTO MARCH TOWARDS RECORD THIRD LEAGUE TITLE.

text.p: Porto extended their lead at the top of the Portuguese first division to a virtually unassailable 11 points on Sunday, beating Leca 2-1 at home as Lisbon rivals Sporting and Benfica faltered.
Benfica, mid-week conquerors of Porto in a Portuguese Cup semifinal, squandered a fine chance to narrow the gap with second-placed Sporting when they were held to a 0-0 home draw by Rio Ave.
Sporting, who look likely to be Benfica's Cup rivals in a replay of last year's final, gave one of their worst performances of the season in losing 1-0 away to Uniao de Leiria.
With just five games to go, reigning champions Porto have 73 points, ahead of Sporting on 62 and Benfica 55.

Porto, whose coach Antonio Oliveira was rushed to hospital with heart problems on Saturday, opened the scoring in the 27th minute when defender Joao Manuel Pinto forced the ball home after Leca's Yugoslav Stoijkovic Vladan failed to hold on to a free-kick from Serbian winger Ljubimko Drulovic.
Brazilian Edmilson Poimenta made it 2-0 minutes later when he converted a penalty.
Leca's consolation goal came when a weakly struck back pass from Porto captain Jorge Costa was seized on by Leca striker Constantino Jardim.
Sporting wasted a number of chances and eventually paid for their extravagance when, with just nine minutes to go, Joao Manuel rose above the Sporting defence to head home from a corner.
Benfica's best chance came in the 35th minute when the referee awarded them a penalty. But Brazilian midifielder Valdo Filho missed with his spot kick.
